diagnosis_explanation:
You had surgery to replace your right hip.

You have some pain in your right leg. This can happen after hip surgery. You also have some muscle spasms in your calf.

You may feel more tired than usual. This is because your body has fewer red blood cells right now. This is called anemia.

You also have some pain. We will help manage this pain.

You have arthritis in your joints. This is a common problem as people age.

You have feelings of sadness or worry. This is also called depression and anxiety. We will help you manage this.

You will keep taking medicine to help prevent blood clots. This is called DVT prophylaxis.

You will also take medicine to protect your stomach. This is GI prophylaxis.
medication_rationale:
Paxil:
This medicine helps with depression and anxiety.
It can help you feel more even.
You might feel sleepy or tired.
You may also have an upset stomach.
Call your doctor if you have thoughts of hurting yourself.

MOBIC:
This medicine helps reduce pain and swelling.
It is for your hip pain after surgery.
You may have an upset stomach or heartburn.
Call your doctor if you get stomach pain or dark, tarry stools.

Klonopin:
This medicine helps with anxiety.
It can also help you sleep.
You may feel drowsy or dizzy.
Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.

Celebrex:
This medicine helps with pain and swelling.
It is given for arthritis pain.
You may get an upset stomach.
Call your doctor if you have stomach pain or black, tarry stools.

Coumadin:
This medicine helps prevent blood clots.
It is important after your surgery.
You may bruise or bleed more easily.
Call your doctor if you notice blood in your urine or stool.
Call your doctor if you get severe headaches.

Colace:
This medicine helps soften your stools.
This makes it easier to have a bowel movement.
You may get mild stomach cramps.
This is usually not a reason to worry.

Fiorinal:
This medicine helps with pain.
It is a pain reliever.
You may feel sleepy or dizzy.
Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.

Oxycodone 20 mg:
This medicine helps manage severe pain.
It is a strong pain reliever.
You may feel sleepy or very dizzy.
You may feel sick to your stomach.
Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.

Oxycodone 5 mg:
This medicine helps manage pain as needed.
It is a strong pain reliever.
You may feel sleepy or very dizzy.
You may feel sick to your stomach.
Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing.

Protonix:
This medicine helps lower the acid in your stomach.
This can prevent stomach upset.
You may get a headache.
This is usually not a reason to worry.

Dulcolax suppository:
This medicine helps you have a bowel movement.
It is used when you need it.
You may get stomach cramps.
This is usually not a reason to worry.

Lactulose:
This medicine helps soften your stools.
It makes it easier to have a bowel movement.
You may get gas or stomach upset.
This is usually not a reason to worry.

Arixtra:
This medicine helps prevent blood clots.
It is given after your surgery.
You may notice redness or bruising at the injection site.
Call your doctor if you have signs of bleeding.

Feosol:
This medicine provides iron for your body.
It helps treat anemia, which is low red blood cells.
You may have an upset stomach or dark stools.
This is usually not a reason to worry.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will feel tired and sore after surgery.
- Rest is important this week.
- You can walk short distances inside your home.
- Use your walker or crutches as shown in therapy.
- Do not put any weight on your right leg.
- Do not bend your right hip more than 90 degrees.
- Avoid crossing your legs.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 101F.

**Week 2:**
- Your pain should start to get a little better.
- You may feel a bit more energy each day.
- Continue walking short distances inside your home.
- Keep using your walker or crutches.
- Keep avoiding bending your right hip past 90 degrees.
- Do not cross your legs.
- Your goal is to walk a little farther each day.
- Call your doctor if your surgical cut looks red or has pus.

**Week 3:**
- You may feel less pain and more comfort.
- You can start to do more light activities at home.
- You can walk around your home without your walker.
- Use a cane for walking if your doctor or therapist says so.
- Keep avoiding bending your right hip past 90 degrees.
- Do not cross your legs.
- Your goal is to walk for 5 to 10 minutes, 2 to 3 times a day.
- Call your doctor if you have sudden, severe pain in your hip.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel more comfortable and have more energy.
- You can start to walk outside on flat surfaces.
- You can walk for up to 15 minutes at a time.
- Continue to avoid bending your right hip past 90 degrees.
- Do not cross your legs.
- Your goal is to walk outside every day for 15 minutes.
- Call your doctor if you notice swelling or redness in your calf.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You will likely feel better week by week.
- Full recovery can take several months.
- Keep doing your physical therapy exercises.
- Follow all your doctor's activity instructions.
- Attend all follow-up appointments.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Calf pain or leg swelling: You may have a blood clot.
- Wound looks infected: Red streaks mean infection is spreading.
- Cannot keep fluids down: You are losing too much fluid.
- Severe pain not helped by medicine: Your pain is out of control.
- Fever above 101 degrees: You may have a bad infection.
- Waking up confused or very sleepy: Your brain may be affected.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Questions about pain medicine: Your nurse can help adjust doses.
- Mild redness or swelling at wound: This can happen while you heal.
- Constipation not improving: Your bowel movements may be slow.
- Mild muscle spasms: This can happen after surgery.
- Feeling down or anxious: Your mood may need attention.
- Bleeding gums or nosebleeds: You may have bruising.
